tools.name: mock-generate

tools.description: Manage the mocker's burst/soak load runs against the dev pipeline. Actions: list, start, status (id required), cancel (id required). start requires mode, target, businessId, payloadSource, ratePerSecond — plus total for a burst or durationMinutes for a soak. Every numeric limit (rate, burst total, soak duration) is advisory in three tiers: below 'warn' it's silent; above 'warn' it proceeds with a `warnings` array in the response; above 'confirm' the start is REJECTED with HTTP 409 and `{needsConfirmation: true, warnings: [...]}` — read the warnings and resend the exact same call with `confirm: true` to actually start it. A 'hard max' tier exists per field (sized at 'would plausibly take shared dev Snap/collector/dedupe down') and always rejects — no confirm bypasses it. Only ONE run may be active at a time (a second start returns 'a run is already in progress'). Dev-only — requires MOCKER_STAGING_URL + MOCKER_STAGING_KEY.

businessId.description: start: dev business to send as (e.g. 'GADG')

confirm.description: start: pass true to proceed after a prior start returned needsConfirmation:true for these same values

correlationId.description: start: an optional correlation-id PREFIX for the run — every message becomes '<prefix>-<n>', so one Datadog query covers the whole run. Kept mock-identifiable. Defaults to 'mock-run-<runId>'.

durationMinutes.description: start, soak only: run length in minutes — advisory tiers (warn/confirm/hard-max), see tool description

mode.description: start: burst = fixed message count as fast as the rate allows; soak = steady rate for a duration

payloadSource.description: Where each send's payload comes from: freshly generated per send, or a saved preset

orderClass.description: Sets order.class — per-business, some Snap tenants require one (GADW works for GADG); omit to leave unset

skus.description: SKUs to put on the generated lines

ratePerSecond.description: start: messages/second, fired concurrently once per second regardless of mode — advisory tiers (warn/confirm/hard-max), same for burst and soak (see tool description)

recordType.description: Required for the cross-entity targets, omit for the legacy per-entity ones. create_record_request/create_record: sales_order | purchase_order | master_data | return_goods_authorization | work_order. confirmation_ready: pick_confirmation | pack_confirmation | return_goods_authorization | dispatch | receipt | finished_good_receipt | work_order_confirmation.

broadcast.description: confirmation_ready only: stamp the planned broadcast attribute (the customer-level broadcast opt-in)

channel.description: The origin channel to impersonate. Stamped as metadata.source, always mock-marked so mock traffic is never mistaken for a real ingest: 'mock-sftp' / 'mock-rest' / 'mock-shopify', or plain 'mock' when omitted. Also auto-resolves metadata.connectorId to the customer's first connector of that type unless connectorId is given.

connectorId.description: The originating connector to attribute the record to — stamped as metadata.connectorId, the fine-grained key smart confirmation routing (FUSE-927) routes on. Use it to target a SPECIFIC connector when a customer has several of the same type (channel alone cannot distinguish them), or pass an unknown id to exercise the connector-unresolvable broadcast path. Omit BOTH connectorId and channel to mock a manual-Snap-origin record (no originating connector — the broadcast path).

target.description: Which dev Pub/Sub topic to address — the three cross-entity topics take a recordType; the two legacy per-entity confirmation topics do not

total.description: start, burst only: total messages — advisory tiers (warn/confirm/hard-max), see tool description

tools.name: mock-schedule

tools.description: One-off publish of a mock canonical message onto a Fuse DEV Pub/Sub topic via fuse-mocker. The payload is passed through the mocker's canonical validation gate and published in a proper Bifrost envelope (correlationId minted, metadata.source always mock-marked — 'mock', or 'mock-<channel>' when a channel is chosen). Returns { correlationId, messageId, topic }; a 400 response carries the canonical-validation issues verbatim. Use mock-generate first if you need a payload built from the customer's real config. To exercise smart confirmation routing, set options.connectorId to a specific originating connector (or omit it for the manual-origin broadcast path). Dev-only — requires MOCKER_STAGING_URL + MOCKER_STAGING_KEY; there is no production mocker.

businessId.description: Dev business the message belongs to (e.g. 'GADG')

correlationId.description: An optional correlation id of your own (e.g. 'perf-test-7') so you can trace this send in Fuse's logs without copying a generated uuid. Kept mock-identifiable — prefixed 'mock-' unless it already starts with it. Reuse the same value across sends to group them under one trace, then read them back with mock-activity's correlationId filter. Charset: letters, digits, . _ : -

channel.description: The origin channel to impersonate. tools.name: mock-send

tools.description: Fetch one held failure by id — the canonical record as stored, envelope metadata, failure stage/source/errors, replay history, and the replayability verdict. Read this before retrying: `replayable` runs the same strict canonical schema the retry gate runs, and `blockingIssues` lists the field/problem pairs that would reject it. The id is replay-service's own UUID, not a Mongo _id. Requires REPLAY_SERVICE_STAGING_URL + REPLAY_SERVICE_STAGING_KEY (and/or PRODUCTION equivalents).
tools.name: replay-get-failure

tools.description: List the failures replay-service holds — the pipeline's failure inbox — paged and newest first. Filter by business, record type, whether the failure has ever been replayed (replayed: false is the untried queue, true is 'failed again'), a substring search over the record reference and failure reason, or a creation date. Each summary carries recordId, reason, attempts, lastReplayAt and lastReplayStatus. Requires REPLAY_SERVICE_STAGING_URL + REPLAY_SERVICE_STAGING_KEY (and/or PRODUCTION equivalents).

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 date — matches that whole day, not a range (e.g. '2026-08-18')

replayed.description: true = replayed at least once and failed again; false = never replayed

search.description: Case-insensitive substring over the record reference and failure reason

useCase.description: Restrict to one or more record types

tools.name: replay-list-failures

tools.description: Retry (redrive) one held failure by id — republishes the stored canonical record so it re-enters the pipeline, and appends the attempt to the failure's replay history. Inbound record types re-enter at ingress via their create_*_request topic and are deduped downstream, so a double retry is safe; confirmation record types go to confirmation_ready. The record must pass the strict canonical schema first — a fresh failure is stored as a deep partial and usually needs repairing (via the Retry Queue in fuse-ui) before it will retry, so check replay-get-failure's blockingIssues first. Requires REPLAY_SERVICE_STAGING_URL + REPLAY_SERVICE_STAGING_KEY (and/or PRODUCTION equivalents). Production retries require confirm: true.

actor.description: Who to attribute the attempt to in the replay history (e.g. an email); defaults to 'fuse-mcp'

confirm.description: Must be true when retrying in production

tools.name: replay-retry

tools.description: Submit canonical data to Fuse via the fapi v2 API. Authenticates as the business itself: resolves the business's REST connector apiKey from config-service and sends HTTP Basic auth (businessId:apiKey), matching fapi's RemoteConfigApiKeyGuard. Requires FAPI_{ENV}_URL plus CONFIG_SERVICE_{ENV}_{URL,KEY} env vars. Production submissions require confirm: true.

businessId.description: The business to submit as (e.g. 'GADG'). Must own a REST connector and match the businessId on every record.

confirm.description: Must be true when submitting to production

payload.description: The canonical record, or an array of records. A single object is wrapped into an array for the v2 bulk endpoint.
